answer: Cross-history contradiction checks. Each identity must sign every transcript entry with its own quill and keep an append-only local history. When two identities interact, each must counter-sign a bridge record containing the other’s latest history head. A cloned identity cannot answer two conflicting bridge records unless it forks state; identical clones collide on the same head, while forked copies need separate keys, storage, and continuous signing work. Any contradiction triggers a willow dispute file that locks both identities pending manual audit.
